draft.title: Australia's urban pattern
card: Australia is one of the most urbanised countries in the world. This means that most of its people live in towns and cities, not in rural areas.
Most Australians live in a few large capital cities, such as Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth. Most of these cities are on or near the coast.

In most states, the capital is far bigger than the next largest town. For example, Melbourne has several million people, while Victoria's next largest cities, such as Geelong and Ballarat, are much smaller.
Large parts of the inland have very few people. The population is packed into a small share of the land, mainly along the coast.
draft.remember: Australia's people are mostly in a few big coastal capitals, each far larger than any other town in its state.

a.q: Which statement best describes where most Australians live?
opts: In a few large capital cities near the coast
In many small towns spread across the inland
On farms and stations in rural areas
In several equal-sized cities across the country
a.why: Most Australians live in a few big capital cities, mostly near the coast. The inland has few people, so towns spread across it do not hold most of the population.
a.clue: Think about the capitals and where they sit.

b.q: Mia looks at a map of Victoria. Melbourne has about five million people. Geelong has a few hundred thousand. What does this show about Victoria?
opts: The capital is far bigger than the next city
Victoria has no large cities at all
Geelong is nearly as big as Melbourne
Most Victorians live in the inland countryside
b.why: Melbourne is many times larger than Geelong, which matches the pattern of a capital far bigger than the next town. Geelong is much smaller, so it is not close to Melbourne in size.
